objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient who presents with chronic joint pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I’m a 69-year-old man, and over the past several years I’ve had progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees. It gets worse when I’m active and improves when I rest.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any small, raised bumps on your skin that have a tiny indentation or a "dimple" in the center?
turns.patient_answer: I haven’t noticed any small raised skin bumps with a dimple in the center. I’ve mainly been dealing with the pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and eases with rest.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you need to urinate more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: I haven’t noticed that I’m urinating more often than usual. My main issue is the pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that flares with activity and feels better when I rest.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or lacking your usual strength lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t felt generally weak or lacking my usual strength. My main problem is still the progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that’s worse with activity and better with rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any difficulty with dressing yourself lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t had any difficulty dressing myself; I can manage my clothes normally. My main limitation is pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that’s worse with activity and better when I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores appearing specifically along the veins in your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores along the veins in my arms. My main concern is the progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that gets worse with activity and improves with rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itchiness on your skin?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any itchiness on my skin. My main problem remains the progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that gets worse with activity and improves with rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any pain or cramping in your calves when you walk that goes away once you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I don’t really get cramping or pain in my calves when I walk that improves once I stop; it’s mainly the pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and gets better with rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed if your stools have become unusually pale, clay-colored, or light in color recently?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any unusually pale or clay-colored stools; my main issue is still the pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that gets worse with activity and improves with rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any weakness in your hands, such as difficulty gripping objects or a tendency to drop things?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any weakness in my hands—I can grip objects normally and I haven’t been dropping things. My main ongoing problem is still the progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that flares with activity and improves when I rest.”

turns.doctor_question: During these shaking episodes, are you able to remain conscious and aware of your surroundings, or do you lose consciousness?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I don’t recall having any shaking episodes, so I haven’t had to deal with whether I stay conscious or lose consciousness. My symptoms have been mainly the progressively worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees that gets worse with activity and better with rest.
